cards.source_title: Designing AI systems for human leverage and why models cannot architect
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: NEED HUMAN TO DESIGN THE ARCHITECTURE
cards.claim: The AI can read huge codebases, propose design options, outline plans and rip out the changes, but a human must design the architecture.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion list of what AI can and cannot do; no experiment cited in this tweet.
cards.landing: Phase routine: keep an explicit human-owned architecture step before the plan, and let agent steps run unattended after it.

cards.source_title: Designing AI systems for human leverage and why models cannot architect
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: might need human to fiddle with the order to make it hands-on testable during the build
cards.claim: Ordering a plan into milestones that are incrementally testable is a second human-needed step, because coding RL such as SWE-bench-multilingual does not teach it.
cards.evidence_detail: Claim about training signal; no data given.
cards.landing: Ship plan phase design: a human or owner check on milestone order and testability before a phase starts.

cards.source_title: Designing AI systems for human leverage and why models cannot architect
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you're splicing A and B into every other step
cards.claim: Yolo back-and-forth with the agent splices human design and ordering work into every step; better to let the AI run and plug the human in only where needed.
cards.evidence_detail: Workflow argument, anecdotal.
cards.landing: One-phase-per-session routine: batch human decisions at the start (plan) rather than interleaving them.

cards.source_title: Designing AI systems for human leverage and why models cannot architect
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: we need to get clever with new evals and benchmarks
cards.claim: Making models good at architecture and incremental testability needs new evals; he follows SlopCodeBench for this.
cards.evidence_detail: Pointer to SlopCodeBench; no numbers in the tweet.
cards.landing: Evidence base for effort-routing and verifier choices (links to his SlopCodeBench reports).

cards.source_title: AI for code is a deeply technical engineering craft
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: more tokens wont save you, more thinking + skill + llm intuition will
cards.claim: Using AI for coding is a technical craft, and spending more tokens does not substitute for skill and judgment.
cards.evidence_detail: Opinion, says he has said it for about 9 months; 646 likes, no data.
cards.landing: Supports routing effort by task rather than defaulting verifiers to maximum effort.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Agents are code rotators.
cards.claim: A coding agent rotates a mash-up of your code and its SWE-bench-shaped weights into new code according to the prompt, so the right mental model is not a junior engineer.
cards.evidence_detail: Mental-model metaphor, no test.
cards.landing: Framing for CLAUDE.md content: the code and prompt dominate, so context in the repo matters more than persona text.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Go prove the code works the way you say it does.
cards.claim: Learning tests are bundled unit tests that prove properties of an external system and are kept out of the normal suite, run only when verifying that system.
cards.evidence_detail: Practice description in a reply to a proofs-mode suggestion.
cards.landing: A tagged, normally-skipped test class for facts about Supabase/R2/Expo that CLAUDE.md currently asserts in prose; could back the cold-resume frozen facts.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: By the end of 2026 the bash tool will be considered harmful.
cards.claim: A deterministic set of about 20-30 predefined commands (like make tasks) beats free bash for anything but the most greenfield projects.
cards.evidence_detail: Prediction; no measurement.
cards.landing: A fixed make/script command set with capped output as the agent's verification surface; re-opens the skipped hooks/pre-commit-gate idea in a lighter form.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I don't care if the model reviews the code and says it's good.
cards.claim: He distrusts LLM assessment of code and cares only whether tests pass; good deterministic feedback loops are a bar for design partners.
cards.evidence_detail: Stated policy, no data.
cards.landing: Argues against reviewer-agent-only gates; ties each PR claim to a failing-then-passing test (already fail-before/pass-after in the routine).

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: easier to read a couple of good black box integration tests
cards.claim: A few black-box integration tests serving as the specification are easier for a human to read than reviewing all the code.
cards.evidence_detail: Review-economy argument, no numbers.
cards.landing: Owner view and cold-resume trial could lean on black-box tests as the readable spec.

cards.source_title: The context-engineering continuum for harder features
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: more context engineering == you can ship bigger features in spicier codebases
cards.claim: The more context engineering applied, the bigger the feature and the harder the codebase an agent can handle.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line claim, 77 likes, no data.
cards.landing: Scale context effort to feature difficulty rather than one routine for every phase.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: self-forking agents is a cool new paradigm
cards.claim: An agent that resets itself to a known checkpoint with a summary or instruction (kimi-cli's D-Mail) is a promising new context-management paradigm.
cards.evidence_detail: Endorsement of a pattern shown by @darrenangle; no measurement.
cards.landing: Mid-phase checkpoint-and-rewind instead of compaction; links to his Context Forking post.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: RPI is a more tactical/practical approach that is downstream from specification
cards.claim: Spec-driven development is a broader category including making outcomes verifiable for feedback loops; RPI is a narrower tactic downstream of it and should not be folded under the label.
cards.evidence_detail: Terminology argument.
cards.landing: Phase routine vocabulary: separate the spec (with verifiable outcomes) from the research-plan-implement tactics.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the mechanism under the hood is obfuscated from the driver
cards.claim: Some compactors hide what they keep, which suits vibe coding but is bad for context engineering; explicit handoff documents (agent's 'last will') work better.
cards.evidence_detail: Agrees with @schickling's experience; no numbers.
cards.landing: Supports one-phase-per-session with written handoff over default compaction; the PR decisions journal is already a handoff.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: whenever an LLM tells me something is good or bad, I become immediately skeptical.
cards.claim: Evaluative statements from the model usually come from accidental steering or sycophancy; the useful output is neutral statements of fact, and he clears context and restarts when he sees evaluations.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal observation, no counts.
cards.landing: Refuter/reviewer prompts: ask for neutral findings with evidence rather than good/bad verdicts; restart context on evaluative drift.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: super helpful for mental alignment with the agent (and with the team) before writing the actual plan
cards.claim: Having the agent produce a component tree before planning a refactor aligns human and agent on structure and removes complex state and useEffects.
cards.evidence_detail: Personal use; image of the tree not captured here.
cards.landing: A pre-plan structural diagram step for the web manager's React Context state; could become a skill.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: type errors -> truth errors
cards.claim: If specs are the code, debugging is finding the one line of incorrect context in research and plan markdown, and test suites should check truth and logical consistency of those documents.
cards.evidence_detail: Conceptual argument building on @sgrove's idea.
cards.landing: Consistency checks on plan/knowledge-store documents; a cold-resume trial that catches a wrong frozen fact is a truth-error test.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: you go upstream, fix the spec, and restart the *implementation*
cards.claim: When a step-through of an implementation reveals a spec error, fix the spec upstream and restart the implementation rather than patching code.
cards.evidence_detail: Debugging heuristic.
cards.landing: Phase routine rule: a failed phase edits the plan at its sha and reruns in a fresh session, not patch-on-patch.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: more and more "compilation" will be unattended
cards.claim: Spec compilation will increasingly run unattended, with less diff-by-diff watching and more spec in, code out.
cards.evidence_detail: Prediction; he later argues against lights-off factories in July 2026 essays.
cards.landing: Context for how much unattended running the plan permits; compare with his later 2-3x position.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Claude subagents are context management + prompt shortcuts. That is all.
cards.claim: Using subagents to play house with anthropomorphised roles fails; they are for context management and prompt shortcuts only.
cards.evidence_detail: Strong opinion; says engineers who do this well are 100x more effective, no data.
cards.landing: Custom-agent design: define agents by context isolation and a reusable prompt (like the Haiku locator), not by role personas.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: fable 5 did a +5k/-5k refactor on our oldest messiest react code
cards.claim: One roughly 2-hour Fable 5 session produced a 5k-line-in, 5k-line-out refactor with no apparent regressions and about 80% of decisions he agreed with.
cards.evidence_detail: Diff size, 2hr duration and 80% agreement are self-reported; regressions still being checked with manual and browser testing.
cards.landing: Reference run for a large refactor phase: queue-driven, compact between steps, human skims diffs.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: keeping a queue of ~5-7 messages until the end.
cards.claim: He queued the prompts as separate messages, added more about every 20 minutes while skimming diffs, and interleaved /compact between prompts to keep context small.
cards.evidence_detail: Shown prompt chain: refactor to under 500 lines, /compact, make it cleaner, /no-use-effect skill, remove prop drilling.
cards.landing: A saved, parameterised prompt-queue workflow with compaction between steps; contrast with fresh session per phase.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: It did not have the taste to do some things until i explicitly steered it.
cards.claim: The model lacked taste: it added react-context (hiding complexity) and spread-operator hacks, and only reduced prop drilling and effects when told.
cards.evidence_detail: Specific failures listed from one session.
cards.landing: Relevant to the web manager's single React Context (AppContext.jsx) design rule and to review checklists on code quality; steering belongs in explicit prompts or skills.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: /no-use-effect (our skill to read the react docs and remove unnecessary use effects)
cards.claim: A small skill that reads authoritative docs and applies one narrow rule (remove unnecessary effects) was reused repeatedly in the refactor.
cards.evidence_detail: Named skill used twice in the prompt chain.
cards.landing: Model for new project skills: narrow, doc-grounded, invoked repeatedly.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: create a giant html canvas with collapsible sub nodes
cards.claim: For review he asked the agent for a collapsible hierarchical HTML walkthrough of the refactor, optimised for human consumption.
cards.evidence_detail: Final prompt in the chain; precursor of his /show-me skill.
cards.landing: Owner-view format: generated hierarchical page for large diffs instead of reading raw PRs.

cards.source_title: Fable 5 refactor write-up (oldest messiest React code)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: easier to vibe code frontend because you can see it
cards.claim: Frontend code quality deteriorates faster under vibe coding because the result is visible, so regressions creep into poorly factored code; React's real mental model is very deep.
cards.evidence_detail: Aside observation, no data.
cards.landing: Caution for the web manager phases: visible-output approval is a weak quality gate.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: they're mostly just well-engineered software with LLM capabilities integrated at key points
cards.claim: Successful production AI systems are mostly ordinary well-engineered software with small focused LLM loops inserted, not a prompt plus a bag of tools.
cards.evidence_detail: Based on trying many frameworks and talking to founders; no counts.
cards.landing: Justifies deterministic scripts around agents (saved workflows) rather than free-form agent runs.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I always thought of it more as a "wish list"
cards.claim: 12-factor agents is a wish list of what the community wants from agent tools, not a hit piece on frameworks.
cards.evidence_detail: Clarification of intent, anecdotal.
cards.landing: Low relevance to the harness; context on how to read his anti-framework stance.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: "refactor AFTER patterns emerge". its a good policy
cards.claim: None of the hot agent frameworks are used in the top coding agents, which are now adding framework-like features; abstract only after patterns emerge.
cards.evidence_detail: Observation across opencode, Codebuff and Claude Code; no data.
cards.landing: Policy for the workflow library: save a workflow only after the same script shape has recurred.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: get you a coding agent that lets you inspect and iterate on subagent prompts
cards.claim: A coding agent should let the user inspect and iterate on the prompts it sends to subagents.
cards.evidence_detail: One-line wish.
cards.landing: Log delegated subagent prompts verbatim so they can be inspected and reused; helps tell whether a routine was followed.

cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: if you're building greenfield, just write the specs and use ralph
cards.claim: Research/plan/implement is for brownfield codebases; greenfield work should be specs plus a Ralph loop.
cards.evidence_detail: Two-line heuristic, 14 replies not captured.
cards.landing: Choose the routine by repo maturity: FixFlow is brownfield (42 tables, three runtimes) so phased research/plan fits; new isolated slices could use spec-plus-loop.
